task.description: Write test/specs/REQ-024.md and ExUnit tests under test/letflow/ for Letflow.EventStore.Registry, covering all 5 acceptance criteria. This module does real DB work (schema-per-tenant, like REQ-022) -- reuse REQ-022's established test patterns for tenant provisioning + Sandbox mode where needed (test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs is your reference). The JSON Schema validator (json_schema.ex) is pure and should get its own thorough test coverage independent of the DB-backed registry functions -- test the 8 supported keywords (type, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, enum, required, properties, items, additionalProperties) plus the 'unsupported keywords are permitted and inert' behavior directly.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains an event_type_registry migration (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022) applying cleanly
register_type/2 rejects a second registration with the same (name, schema_version) with a distinct, testable error, not a generic changeset failure
validate_payload/2 against a payload missing a required field returns a failure result whose detail names the specific field_path (JSON Pointer form) and constraint, not just a boolean false
get_type/1 against an unregistered name returns an explicit :unknown_event_type-shaped error rather than nil or an exception
the moduledoc names the JSON Schema validation library choice as an explicit open question for CODE-DESIGNER, not a silently made decision

result.summary:
Wrote test/specs/REQ-024.md and two new ExUnit test files covering all 5 acceptance criteria, split per the task's own instruction between the pure JSON Schema validator and the DB-backed Registry context module. Read all mandatory inputs first: registry.ex/event_type.ex/json_schema.ex/validation_failure.ex, lib/letflow/design/req024-event-type-registry.md (full, including rework-iteration-1's tenant_id-not-prefix correction), test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs (REQ-022's DB-backed schema-per-tenant pattern), test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs (REQ-028's per-keyword pure-validator style), and both ELIXIR-DEV's (step-02a) and REVIEWER's (step-02d) prior handoffs for this run, including ELIXIR-DEV's two self-flagged issues (the untested DB-level unique-constraint backstop, and the migration-module-loading gap).

test/letflow/event_store/registry/json_schema_test.exs (NEW, 45 tests, async: true, zero DB/I-O dependency): one describe block per each of the 8 supported keyword families (type, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, enum, required, properties, items, additionalProperties) plus the 'unsupported keywords are permitted and inert' contract (a $ref/pattern/format/allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/patternProperties/dependencies/title/description keyword-salad schema, payload deliberately violating what pattern WOULD enforce, accepted), RFC 6901 pointer construction (root '/' rendering, '~0'/'~1' escaping, nested+indexed composition), the type-mismatch cascade-avoidance short-circuit (stops sibling checks at that level, not sibling subtrees), and the 'reports every violation, not just the first' requirement (ES-05). Found and fixed two of my own test-design bugs before this was correct: (1) a top-level non-map-payload test was calling validate/2's own is_map guard incorrectly -- rewrote to exercise the guarded nested-value case instead; (2) a 3-simultaneous-violation test asserted a specific cross-key Map-iteration order that isn't part of the algorithm's documented contract (only the required-before-properties structural ordering is guaranteed by object_violations/3's fixed call order) -- fixed to assert the guaranteed part directly and the rest via MapSet, with the reasoning documented in test/specs/REQ-024.md's 'Map-iteration-order caution' section.

test/letflow/event_store/registry_test.exs (NEW, 28 tests, async: false, DIRECTIVE T-1 real Postgres via a provisioned_tenant/1 setup helper mirroring tenant_provisioning_test.exs's :auto-mode + on_exit cleanup pattern exactly, since event_type_registry is tenant-scoped and only exists after a real replay_migrations/2 call): AC1 (migration applies cleanly under a real provisioned tenant's own schema, absent from public, correct columns via information_schema) -- 1 test. AC2 (register_type/2) -- 7 tests: successful registration + real-Postgres persistence check, the literal AC2 duplicate-rejection case, the Letflow-specific :schema_version_not_monotonic rule (distinct atom from :duplicate_event_type_version) plus its positive boundary, 4 changeset-level rejections (empty name, >128 chars, schema_version 0, explicit-nil json_schema -- deliberately NOT Map.delete, since the field's own `default: %{}` masks an omitted key from validate_required/2, a real gotcha I hit and documented), :tenant_not_provisioned, and -- addressing ELIXIR-DEV's own flagged gap -- a genuine concurrent-race test forcing two Task-spawned register_type/2 calls for the IDENTICAL (name, schema_version) past a message-passing barrier so only the table's real unique index (not the app-level pre-check, which both calls pass) decides the winner; asserts exactly one {:ok,_}/one {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} (never a leaked raw changeset) plus a direct Postgres COUNT(*) confirming exactly one row. AC3 (validate_payload/3) -- 9 tests: the literal AC3 required-field-with-field_path case, 3 more keyword examples (minLength/enum/type) through the real DB-backed wiring, inert-keyword end-to-end permissiveness, a fully-valid-payload happy path, malformed-JSON and non-object-root-JSON both producing field_path '/'/constraint 'type', unknown-event-type propagation, most-recent-schema_version selection (v1 permissive/v2 strict, empty payload rejected only under v2), :tenant_not_provisioned. AC4 (get_type/2) -- 5 tests: unknown name -> explicit error never nil/exception (both forms asserted), single version, multiple versions returns numerically highest (registered out-of-sequence as 1/2/5, not just 1/2/3, to rule out 'most recent insert' or 'row count' false positives), :tenant_not_provisioned, and a tenant-isolation test beyond the bare ACs (event type registered for tenant A is invisible to independently-provisioned tenant B). AC5: verified by direct inspection of registry.ex's shipped @moduledoc (lines 33-55, the '## JSON Schema validation library choice' section) -- confirmed present, no runtime test, matching REQ-020 AC5/REQ-022 AC4 precedent; also directly grep-confirmed ex_json_schema absent from mix.exs/mix.lock (exit 1, no match).

During development this file's own first draft had a real bug (documented in the spec, not hidden): on_exit cleanup was registered AFTER provision_tenant_schema/replay_migrations, so a failure in either step (which is exactly what happened before a separate, genuine production gap was worked around -- see below) left real, :auto-mode-committed orphan Tenant rows/schemas with no cleanup registered. Fixed by moving on_exit registration to immediately after the Tenant row itself commits. Manually cleaned up the orphan data this produced during development via a one-off scratch/-scoped script (deleted afterward, per file-placement rules), verified clean via direct pg_catalog.pg_namespace query before any counted test run.

Separately, hit and worked around (test-file-scoped only, no shipped file touched) the exact functional gap ELIXIR-DEV's own step-02a handoff already flagged as issue 1: priv/repo/migrations/*.exs isn't part of :test's elixirc_paths, and Ecto.Migrator's directory scan skips (never loads) a migration module once its version is already recorded in schema_migrations -- so replay_migrations/2's real tenant_scoped_migrations/0 default (referencing the bare module atom) failed to resolve it. Fixed via Code.require_file/1 on the real migration file (path-expanded from __DIR__, not hardcoded), mirroring the identical technique ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff already used for its manual AC1 demonstration. This exercises the REAL migration file, not a stand-in fixture. The underlying gap is pre-existing production risk already flagged in ELIXIR-DEV's issues list for a future fix -- not re-filed as a duplicate here.

Verification (mix 1.20.3 / Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29, real Postgres on localhost:5462, no Docker fallback needed): `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` -> 'Result: 73 passed' (28 + 45). Flakiness check on the concurrency test: `mix test test/letflow/event_store/registry_test.exs --seed <1..5>` -> 28/28 passed all 5 runs. `mix format --check-formatted` clean across the whole project (both new files auto-formatted once, verified clean after). Full suite run twice consecutively: `mix test` -> 'Result: 234 passed (4 properties, 230 tests)' both times (234 = pre-existing 161-test baseline + 73 new tests; zero pre-existing test changed status). Direct Postgres query after both full-suite runs (`SELECT nspname FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%'`) returned zero rows, confirming provisioned_tenant/1's on_exit cleanup is genuinely load-bearing, not just claimed. git status --short confirms no stray files outside the three artifacts_out paths.
issues: Not a new issue -- flagging that ELIXIR-DEV's step-02a handoff issue 1 (priv/repo/migrations/*.exs not part of :test's elixirc_paths, so a bare module-atom reference in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 fails to resolve once Ecto.Migrator's directory scan has already recorded that version as applied) is a genuine PRE-EXISTING production risk this test file independently reproduced and worked around at the test-file level only (Code.require_file/1). It remains open for a real fix (e.g. an Application-boot-time require loop, or switching replay_migrations/2 to a directory-scoped Migrator.run call) -- not fixed here since that would mean editing lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex or lib/letflow/application.ex, outside this handoff's owned_modules (test/letflow, test/specs) and outside TEST-DESIGNER's role (tests only, no application code).
